# Frontier Starting Grant

The application project for the Frontier Research Fund Starting Grant that now funds the [[colorectal-metastasis-atlas]]. Awarded on 2025-11-28; grant period 2026-01-01 to 2030-12-31.

## Outcome

Reached: the grant was awarded at 1.48 M EUR over five years. Reporting under the grant continues in [[frontier-interim-report]].

## Current State

- Completed. The award letter and the conditions attached to it are in [[frontier-award-letter-2025]].
- The money pays [[amara-okonkwo]]'s postdoc position from 2026, the incoming spatial postdoc [[owen-mcallister]] from 2027-01-11, Visium HD runs for 40 liver metastases and half of [[kenji-mori]]'s studentship.
- Two reviewer concerns became work: deconvolution at low spot counts ([[deconvolution-benchmark]]) and whether Visium HD resolution suffices (answered by the [[visium-hd-pilot]]).
- Programme manager is [[thabo-nkosi]]; he is the contact for amendments and the interim report.

## Scope and Boundaries

This note covers the application, the interview and the award terms. Atlas science and progress live in the atlas Project and its children. Reporting obligations live in [[frontier-interim-report]].

## Working Context

The proposal was submitted on 2025-03-18 after ten weeks of writing, with preliminary data from the first months of the Visium HD pilot. It passed the first step in July 2025 with scores of 4.5, 4.0 and 3.5 out of 5 ([[frontier-reviewer-reports-2025]]). The third reviewer doubted that low-count spots in necrotic and fibrotic regions could be assigned to cell types reliably; Ines answered at the interview with the design of the benchmark that Kenji had started on 2025-09-01. The panel at the [[frontier-interview-2025-10-14]] spent most of its time on the chemotherapy before/after design and on sample access through the tissue unit run by [[benedikt-kraus]].

What worked: a single clear figure of the atlas design, a named pathologist, and pilot data at real resolution. What did not: the data sharing section was thin and the panel asked twice about the public release plan, which later became the [[atlas-data-portal]] idea.
